title: Docs: Do not install man(1) pages for extcaps and change wireshark-filter section
description:
Extcaps fall into the plugin category and are not in the shell path
so they should not have a man(1) page. They still have HTML manuals.

notes.body: changed title from **Do not install man pages for extcaps and change wireshark-filter section** to **{+Docs: +}Do not install man{+(1)+} pages for extcaps and change wireshark-filter section**

added 6 commits
  • bbea3210...7f32c90a - 4 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • f160868a - Do not install man pages for extcaps
  • 5688bfb8 - Install wireshark-filter man page to section 7
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13688/diffs?diff_id=872940414&start_sha=bbea32102337a1df0186399a0923c8c0e06c852b)

added 1 commit
  • 201c2068 - Install wireshark-filter man page to section 7
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13688/diffs?diff_id=872941727&start_sha=5688bfb8dfbb0c944d2bd2d4ff3520f85c6bf3a4)

I'm leaning against this. Some of our extcaps, sshdump in particular, can be tricky to configure in some cases and I'm guessing that being able to browse through the various options and examples from the command line would be useful.

`man(1)`'s purpose is to provide documentation for the system. In particular man 1 pages are reserved for system commands run using the shell. As a user I find it annoying to have these extensions in my system's commands. If every package did that man would become much less useful for its intended purpose.

commits_data.title: Do not install man pages for extcaps
commits_data.message:
Do not install man pages for extcaps

Extcaps fall into the plugin category and are not in the shell path
so they should not have a man(1) page. They still have HTML manuals.

commits_data.title: Install wireshark-filter man page to section 7
commits_data.message:
Install wireshark-filter man page to section 7

The wireshark-filter man page is currently installed to
section 4 but I have never seen that section used for this.
Wikipedia[1] says this was used with System V but more modern
Unixes have used section 5 for "file formats and conventions", not
section 4.

However wireshark's filter language is not file-related so section
5 also seems wrong. Use section 7 instead (miscellaneous).

[1]https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Man_page#Manual_sections
